subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; exact module variant unresolved here.
subsystems.intake: Two-motor silicone roller and surgical-tubing-held kicker; steep first-event deploy geometry revised after jams.
subsystems.transfer: Roller floor with tape/zip-tie agitation; surgical tubing gave way to grippier surfaces after fuel debris caused slip.
subsystems.scoring: Two-motor feeder, four-X60 drum and powered hood rollers; additional high-speed steel flywheel stores energy in constrained space.
subsystems.endgame: Endgame installation not established by reviewed interview.
subsystems.controls: Battery/current/temperature logging drives changing motor limits; software manages power budget rather than assuming every motor can run unrestricted.

versions: No net at first event; stiff net at second; stretch net by DCMP supports reported 75 capacity.
dossier.analysis: Net compliance affects usable storage, while debris accumulation changes friction over a match. A successful clone needs endurance testing with worn fuel and realistic battery load, not only a short fresh-ball burst.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2026-7558 · Surface contamination, inertia and power control interact
context_documents.body:
# 2026-7558: Surface contamination, inertia and power control interact

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The collector deploy angle was flattened after first-event jams. The retained interview account describes surgical tubing replaced by grippier floor surfaces after fuel debris caused slip. The shooter uses a four-X60 aluminum drum, powered upper rollers and a compact geared steel flywheel; transfer is sequenced after launcher speed is reached. Current, voltage and temperature logging inform operating limits.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team links the added flywheel to reduced speed decay and improved end-of-hopper accuracy. Floor/collector changes respond to observed jamming and contamination, while software limiting responds to the total electrical demand.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A material choice can work with clean practice fuel yet fail when loose surface debris changes friction. A flywheel can smooth a transient without fixing an inadequate recharge rate or a hot motor. The useful design reference is therefore a tested material/contact path plus an explicit electrical budget, not a motor count. Robot logging should distinguish commanded voltage, actual bus voltage, current limit, speed error and fuel flow; otherwise starvation and electrical saturation can look like the same shooting symptom.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Repeat full-hopper tests with used fuel and low batteries. Compare surface cleanliness, slip, speed recovery and motor temperature over multiple shifts rather than a single successful volley.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

source_reviews.title: 7558 ALT F4 Behind the Bumpers
source_reviews.review_basis: Read full publisher description and attempted caption retrieval
source_reviews.facts: Description explicitly identifies autonomous path modes, current control and the ball path as interview topics.
source_reviews.limitations: No readable caption payload retrieved. The published description alone does not support dimensions or design revisions.

source_reviews.title: Retained ALT-F4 interview account
source_reviews.locator: Base robot dossier and focused continuation study
source_reviews.facts: Retained account describes a silicone intake, agitating floor, powered hood, extra flywheel, and load-aware current limits.
source_reviews.limitations: The mechanism claims below are carried forward with this scope. The interview passages themselves were not freshly read.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: ALT-F4’s late robot is described in the retained dossier as a rack collector, extending net bin and powered feed into a wide drum. The newly read interview description corroborates a current-control system and an interview about the ball path, while detailed construction and changes below remain older dossier evidence. The useful question is how friction changes and power management interact. A dirty floor can starve a ready launcher, while a healthy floor can supply fuel faster than the launcher can recover. Both problems can reduce scored output, but they call for different changes.
piece_flow: The retained account traces fuel through the deployable collector and its compliant kicker, into a net-sided hopper.
A powered, agitating floor presents fuel to the feeder. The prior dossier describes replacing slippery contact surfaces after debris accumulated.
A separate feeder stages fuel into a drum and powered hood. Its timing depends on launcher speed according to the older technical study.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The older study describes a steel flywheel separate from the aluminum drum to increase inertia within restricted space. That adds bearing and drive loads and puts service access alongside the normal feed envelope. Stretch netting changes the relationship between maximum packed volume, roof motion and the route the vehicle can drive with a full load. No stowed or loaded dimensions were verified in this review.

subsystems.name: Collector and floor
subsystems.construction: Retained account describes a deployable silicone roller, compliant kicker and powered roller floor.
subsystems.operation: Collect and push the bottom layer forward while agitation redistributes fuel.
subsystems.team_rationale: Older synopsis attributes revised geometry to jamming and revised surfaces to debris-related slip.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Log wheel motion and fuel motion separately. Rotation with stationary fuel identifies lost traction or bridging.
subsystems.interfaces: The collector exit, hopper wall and floor share a region where packed fuel can push back into the mouth.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect debris accumulation during successive shifts and whether floor surfaces are replaceable without extracting the assembly.
subsystems.unknowns: Surface treatment, compression and actual onset of slip.

subsystems.name: Drum and power controls
subsystems.construction: Prior study describes a four-motor drum, powered upper contacts and an auxiliary steel flywheel.
subsystems.operation: Reach speed before feeding, then manage current as other mechanisms run.
subsystems.team_rationale: Prior synopsis attributes the extra inertia to reducing droop.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: More stored energy can improve first-burst uniformity. Sustained firing still depends on energy per shot and the power available while driving.
subsystems.interfaces: Feeder demand, drive draw and thermal or current limits can change launcher readiness simultaneously.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Compare first and last shots under low battery voltage and after motor warm-up.
subsystems.unknowns: Flywheel speed ratio, software thresholds, temperature traces and shot conversion.

revisions: Prior dossier reports a flatter collector deploy geometry after first-event jams.
Prior dossier reports changes from no net to stiff net to stretch net, plus multiple floor-surface revisions.
Prior study attributes a supplemental flywheel to better late-burst consistency. Event installation and ratios are unresolved.
transferable_principles: Measure output by synchronizing release velocity, floor or transfer motion, bus voltage and shot results.
Test material changes with worn fuel and contamination carried over from previous runs.
Compare repeated full-hopper bursts with short demonstrations. Stored inertia and sustained recharge are separate design quantities.
disconfirming_conditions: Added flywheel inertia can hurt if frequent stop and restart cycles dominate or if shaft and belt loads make the launcher less reliable.
A grippier floor can increase wedging if pieces are trapped against stationary walls or if the feeder cannot clear the presented inventory.
remaining_gaps: Full interview captions and independently accessible technical code or write-up remain unverified. Exact current-limit rules, event hardware, measured output and useful capacity remain open.
recommended_images: Interview frames showing the intake-to-floor transition, the auxiliary flywheel mounting and the expanded hopper, pending visual review.
